items.title: Webb telescope spots most primitive galaxy ever found

featured_image.name: James Webb Space Telescope smashes its own record to find the earliest  galaxies that ever existed

items.description:
An international team of astronomers has used the James Webb Space Telescope to characterize the most chemically primitive star-forming galaxy ever observed — an ultra-faint speck of light from 13 billion years ago whose oxygen content is just 1/240th that of the Sun.

The findings, published in Nature on May 13, detail how the team achieved a definitive characterization of the galaxy known as LAP1-B, located at a redshift of 6.625, placing it roughly 800 million years after the Big Bang during the epoch of reionization. The discovery provides what scientists describe as a direct ancestral link to the mysterious "fossil galaxies" found orbiting the Milky Way today.[1][2]

items.title: US clears 10 Chinese firms for Nvidia H200 chips, but no deliveries made

featured_image.name: Watch NVDA Stock Closely: China Comeback Hits Another ...

items.description:
The U.S. Commerce Department has approved roughly 10 Chinese companies to purchase Nvidia H200 artificial intelligence chips, but not a single delivery has taken place, Reuters reported on Thursday, leaving a multibillion-dollar technology deal in limbo as Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang seeks a breakthrough during President Donald Trump's summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing.[1][2][3]

The approved buyers include Alibaba, Tencent, ByteDance, and JD.com, with distributors such as Lenovo and Foxconn also cleared to act as intermediaries, according to three people familiar with the matter. Each approved customer can purchase up to 75,000 chips under U.S. licensing terms. Lenovo confirmed to Reuters that it "is one of several companies approved to sell H200 in China as part of Nvidia's export license".[2][4][1]

items.title: Samsung begins cutting chip output ahead of historic strike

featured_image.name: Samsung holds desperate final talks with union over 18-day chip factory  strike that could cost $20 billion — government-mediated summit seeks to  avert industrial action that could hit HBM production | Tom's Hardware

items.description:
Samsung Electronics has begun reducing semiconductor production ahead of a planned 18-day general strike set to begin on May 21, after marathon government-mediated negotiations collapsed without a deal. The company started cutting chip output on Thursday, according to MoneyToday, as more than 50,000 union workers prepare for what would be the first full shutdown of Samsung's chip fabrication lines in 42 years.[1][2]

The move comes one day after South Korea's Finance Minister Koo Yun-cheol warned that a strike "must not happen under any circumstances," calling it a threat to the country's economic growth, exports, and financial markets. Prime Minister Kim Min-seok convened an emergency meeting of ministers and pledged to "actively support labor-management dialogue so that this does not lead to a strike under any circumstances".[3][4][1]

items.title: Streeting resigns as health secretary, launches bid to unseat Starmer

featured_image.name: Wes Streeting 'preparing to resign' as Keir Starmer dealt leadership blow  moments before King's Speech

items.description:
Wes Streeting resigned as Britain's Health Secretary on Thursday, throwing down a direct challenge to Prime Minister Keir Starmer's leadership of the Labour Party and plunging the governing party deeper into crisis following its disastrous local election results last week.

The BBC confirmed Streeting's resignation on Thursday morning, capping days of speculation after allies had spent Wednesday night phoning Labour MPs to drum up support for a formal leadership contest. The move came just a day after Streeting held a tense, 16-minute meeting with Starmer at Downing Street, following which the Prime Minister insisted he had "full confidence" in his Health Secretary.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Iran demands BRICS condemn US-Israel war at Delhi summit

featured_image.name: Tehran calls on BRICS members to condemn US-Israeli aggression on Iran:  Iranian FM

items.description: Foreign ministers from BRICS nations opened a two-day meeting in New Delhi on Thursday, with the war in Iran launched by the United States and Israel on February 28 dominating the agenda and laying bare fractures within the expanded bloc. The gathering at Bharat Mandapam, chaired by Indian External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar, brings together diplomats from the group's 11 member states — including Iran, the UAE, and Saudi Arabia, countries on opposing sides of the Middle East conflict.[1][2]

items.title: Xi warns Trump of conflict risk if Taiwan is mishandled

featured_image.name: U.S. President Trump Meets With China's President Xi And Attends State Banquet

items.description:
Chinese President Xi Jinping delivered a pointed warning to President Donald Trump on Thursday during their summit in Beijing, saying the two countries risk "clashes and even conflicts" if the Taiwan issue is mishandled, according to a readout published by the official Xinhua news agency.[1]

Xi told Trump that if Taiwan is handled well, US-China relations "will enjoy overall stability," but that failure to do so would put "the entire relationship in great jeopardy," calling Taiwan the "most important issue in China-US relations," according to state broadcaster CCTV.[2][1]

The warning stood in sharp contrast to Trump's warm public remarks at the Great Hall of the People, where the US president told Xi, "You're a great leader. Sometimes people don't like me saying it, but I say it anyway, because it's true." He added, "It's an honor to be with you. It's an honor to be your friend," and predicted the bilateral relationship would be "better than ever before," the Associated Press reported.[1]

items.title: Russia's massive drone attack forces Slovakia to briefly shut Ukraine border

featured_image.name: Slovakia Moves to Close Legal Gaps as Russian Drone Strikes Near Its Border  Raise Alarm” - Robert Lansing Institute

items.description: Slovakia shut down all border crossings with Ukraine on Wednesday afternoon after Russian attack drones struck the western Ukrainian city of Uzhhorod, located just kilometers from the Slovak frontier. The closures, which lasted roughly two hours, came as Russia launched what Ukrainian officials described as one of the largest aerial assaults since the start of the full-scale invasion.

items.title: Trump, Xi open landmark summit in Beijing with calls for cooperation

featured_image.name: Chinese President Xi Jinping gives opening remarks at bilateral talks

items.description:
U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping opened a closely watched bilateral summit at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing on Thursday, exchanging a formal handshake and warm remarks as the leaders of the world's two largest economies sought to project cooperation amid deep divisions over trade, technology, and the war in Iran.

The meeting marks the first visit by a sitting U.S. president to China in nearly nine years, since Trump's own 2017 trip during his first term. Originally planned for April, the summit was postponed due to the U.S. and Israeli military campaign in Iran.[1][2][3]

items.title: Rutte proposes NATO allies spend 0.25% of GDP on Ukraine aid annually

featured_image.name: NATO allies pledge over $21B in Ukraine aid for 2025, Rutte says | Daily  Sabah

items.description:
NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte has proposed that all 32 alliance members commit to spending 0.25% of their gross domestic product each year to support Ukraine, a plan that could nearly triple collective aid to roughly $143 billion annually, according to Politico.[1][2]

Rutte floated the idea at a closed meeting of NATO ambassadors in late April as the alliance prepares for its summer summit in Ankara, Turkey, scheduled for July 7–8. The proposal seeks to put Ukraine support on a more stable and predictable footing while narrowing the gap between high-contributing nations in northern Europe and less generous allies in the south.[2][3]

items.title: UAE denies Netanyahu's claimed secret visit during Iran war

featured_image.name: UAE denies Netanyahu visited in ‘secret’ during US-Israel war on Iran

items.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office announced on Wednesday that he had secretly traveled to the United Arab Emirates during the Israel-U.S. war with Iran and met with UAE President Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed Al Nahyan in Al-Ain on March 26, describing the encounter as an "historic breakthrough" in bilateral relations. Hours later, the UAE's Ministry of Foreign Affairs issued a flat denial, calling any such reports "entirely unfounded."[1][2][3]

items.title: Moscow bans media from publishing drone strike aftermath

featured_image.name: Moscow authorities restrict publication of photos and videos of aftermath  of drone strikes | Reuters

items.description: Moscow's city government has prohibited the publication of photos, videos, and text describing the aftermath of drone strikes and what officials termed "terrorist attacks," extending a pattern of information control that has spread across more than 30 Russian regions since 2025.

items.title: Trump arrives in Beijing for summit with Xi amid Iran war tensions

featured_image.name: WATCH LIVE: Trump and Xi hold meeting as China state visit begins

items.description:
President Donald Trump touched down in Beijing on Wednesday for a high-stakes summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping, arriving against the backdrop of a fragile ceasefire in the Iran conflict and deep uncertainty over whether the two superpowers can find common ground on the Middle East, trade, and Taiwan.

The visit — the first by a U.S. president to China since Trump's own trip in November 2017 — had originally been scheduled for late March but was postponed due to the outbreak of war with Iran in late February. Trump was greeted with a red-carpet welcome ceremony, with Chinese and American flags waved in rhythmic unison by uniformed greeters, according to the Associated Press. The formal bilateral talks between Trump and Xi are set to begin Thursday and extend through Friday.[1][2][3][4][5]

items.title: Iran says Hormuz control could double its oil revenues

featured_image.name: Iran's IRGC navy extends full closure of Strait of Hormuz, ...

items.description: Iranian Army Brigadier General Mohammad Akraminia declared on Wednesday that Tehran's strategic grip over the Strait of Hormuz could generate revenues exceeding twice the country's oil income, as Iran deepens its efforts to formalize control over the world's most vital oil chokepoint amid its ongoing war with the United States and Israel.

items.title: Truck convoys across Arabia become lifeline amid Hormuz closure

featured_image.name: im-68287830?width=700&size=1.501&pixel_ratio=2

items.description:
Convoys of heavy-duty trucks barreling across the Arabian desert have become an unlikely escape valve for the global economy, as the prolonged closure of the Strait of Hormuz forces Gulf states to improvise new land routes for energy and commodity shipments, according to a report published Monday by The Wall Street Journal.[1]

The truck convoys represent one piece of a broader scramble by Saudi Arabia, the UAE, and Oman to keep trade flowing more than two months after Iran effectively shut down the world's most important oil chokepoint in late February, in retaliation for U.S. and Israeli strikes. Before the closure, roughly 20 million barrels of crude oil passed through the strait daily. Traffic has since collapsed to about 5% of pre-war levels, according to maritime data firm Kpler.[2][3]

items.title: Australia joins UK-France naval mission to secure Strait of Hormuz

featured_image.name: Australia bolsters capabilities, training opportunities for its P-8A  aircraft

items.description:
The United Kingdom and France hosted a multinational meeting of defense ministers on Tuesday to advance plans for a naval mission to protect commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, as Australia confirmed it would join the effort and Britain deployed a warship to the region.

UK Defence Secretary John Healey and French Armed Forces Minister Catherine Vautrin co-chaired the virtual meeting, which brought together representatives from more than 40 countries to discuss military contributions to the European-led coalition. The talks came as Iran issued sharp warnings against any foreign naval presence in the waterway.[1][2][3]

items.title: Streeting prepares to resign and challenge Starmer for Labour leadership

featured_image.name: Wes Streeting denies plotting to oust PM Keir Starmer

items.description: Health Secretary Wes Streeting is preparing to resign from the cabinet as early as Thursday to mount a formal leadership challenge against Prime Minister Keir Starmer, according to a report in The Times. The move, which would represent the most direct threat yet to Starmer's premiership, came after Streeting held a brief meeting with the Prime Minister on Wednesday morning ahead of the King's Speech.[1][2][3]

items.title: Trump lands in Beijing, demands China 'open up' to US business

featured_image.name: Live updates: Trump arrives in China for Xi summit

items.description:
President Donald Trump landed in Beijing on Wednesday for a high-stakes state visit, bringing with him a delegation of more than a dozen of America's most powerful corporate executives and a blunt message for Chinese leader Xi Jinping: "open up" China to American firms.[1][2][3]

Trump, who was greeted on the tarmac by Chinese Vice President Han Zheng, a military honor guard, and some 300 flag-waving youths, told reporters aboard Air Force One that market access for U.S. businesses would be his first request when formal talks begin. The summit meetings are scheduled for Thursday and Friday at the Great Hall of the People, with a visit to the Temple of Heaven and a state banquet also planned.[4][5][6][2][1]

items.title: Gunshots erupt at Philippine Senate during ICC arrest standoff

featured_image.name: Bato dela Rosa: Ex-Philippine leader Duterte's drug war enforcer escapes ICC  arrest

items.description:
Gunfire broke out at the Philippine Senate on Wednesday evening as military and law enforcement personnel moved into the building to apprehend Senator Ronald "Bato" dela Rosa, who is wanted by the International Criminal Court on charges of crimes against humanity linked to former President Rodrigo Duterte's deadly anti-drug campaign.[1][2][3]

The identity of those who fired the shots remained unclear as journalists and bystanders scrambled for cover amid the chaos, according to Reuters. The incident marks a dramatic escalation in a standoff that has gripped the country since the ICC unsealed its arrest warrant on Monday.[2]

items.title: Trump arrives in Beijing for first China visit since 2017

featured_image.name: Xi and Trump are heading for tactical stabilisation, not a reset

items.description: President Donald Trump departed Washington on Tuesday for a state visit to China, arriving in Beijing on Wednesday evening for his first trip to the country since 2017 and the first by any sitting U.S. president in nearly nine years. Over the next two days, Trump will hold formal talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping on issues spanning trade, Taiwan, rare earth minerals, artificial intelligence, and the ongoing war in Iran.[1][2]

items.title: Iran restored 30 of 33 Hormuz missile sites, US intel finds

featured_image.name: Iran has likely carried out an undeclared missile test, satellite photos  show

items.description: Classified U.S. intelligence assessments show that Iran has regained operational access to 30 of its 33 missile sites along the Strait of Hormuz and retains roughly 70 percent of its prewar missile stockpile, according to reporting by The New York Times on Monday, sharply undercutting the Trump administration's repeated assertions that the Iranian military had been "decimated."[1][2]
